usuario: Describe a protagonist in 100 to 150 words without mentioning any detail of their physical appearance (no clothes, height, eye or hair color): only through what they do and what they decide.
respuesta: Elena always selects the corner booth at the diner, positioning herself to monitor both exits simultaneously. Before touching her coffee, she checks the salt shaker; if it isn’t completely full, she leaves without paying. Every Tuesday, she transfers half her savings to an anonymous orphanage, then spends the afternoon forging birth certificates for people fleeing violent pasts. When a stranger drops a wallet on the subway, she kicks it under the seat rather than returning it, yet she will miss her own train to help an elderly commuter carry groceries up the stairs. Offered a lucrative promotion that requires relocating, she burns the contract in her kitchen sink. Instead, she adopts a stray dog that bit her the day before. At night, she sleeps with a loaded revolver locked in a safe, hiding the key at the bottom of a fishbowl so she must hesitate before using it.

usuario: Choose an everyday, insignificant object and write a lyric poem of up to twelve lines that treats it as if it were an archaeological treasure or a historic monument.
respuesta:
**Relic of the Forgotten Coast**

Unearthed from beneath the glacial fridge’s shade,
This square of sacred polymer sees the light.
What ancient bakers forged its jagged blade?
What perished fingers snapped its plastic might?
Behold the glyphs of azure, clear and cold:
*Best By the sixth of May*, a vanished year—
A cryptographic prophecy foretold
To guard the golden loaves once gathered here.
Oh, Twin-Toothed Sentinel of daily bread,
You held the twisted throat of life at bay!
Though empires of the pantry long have fled,
Your stoic jaws still bite the air today.

usuario: Choose a complex feeling and define it in up to 120 words using only visual metaphors and textures, without ever using the word that names it. At the end, in square brackets, say which feeling it is.
respuesta:
It is the texture of sun-bleached velvet rubbed against the grain, soft to the touch yet leaving a phantom prickle on the fingertips. It looks like dust motes suspended in a slant of late-afternoon amber light, dancing over a wooden floorboards worn smooth by footsteps that have ceased to walk there. It is the brittle crinkle of a pressed autumn leaf slipping from the creamy, yellowing pages of an old book—delicate, translucent, and threatening to crumble into gold powder if held too tightly. You trace the cold, wavy glass of a rain-streaked windowpane, gazing at a warm, blurred glow in the distance that your hands can never quite reach through the frost. 

[Nostalgia]

usuario: Write a micro-story of 40 to 80 words in which every word begins with the same letter.
respuesta: Seven silent shadows slipped southward. Samuel’s ship sailed swiftly, seeking safe sanctuary. Suddenly, severe storms struck. Savage swells smashed Samuel’s sturdy schooner. Scared sailors shouted, scrambling sideways. Samuel steered steadily, surviving several scary seconds. Soon, sunlight shone softly. Surprised survivors sighted sandy shores. Samuel smiled, savoring sweet safety. Stepping seaward, seven salty sailors sought shelter, sharing stories, singing simple songs, sleeping soundly.

usuario: Write a tense scene of up to 150 words between two characters in which one interrogates the other without using a single question mark: they must get the information using only statements or psychological manipulation.
respuesta:
Miller set the damp photograph on the metal table. He didn’t sit, letting his shadow fall across Julian’s trembling hands. 

"They found your brother’s car by the river, Julian. The trunk was empty, which means the ledger is still in play."

Julian stared at the floor, his jaw clenched tight.

"Loyalty is admirable," Miller continued, his voice dangerously soft. "Right up until the moment you realize Marcus already bought his plane ticket. One seat. First class to Zurich."

Julian’s eyes snapped up, widening just a fraction. 

"There it is," Miller whispered, leaning in. "He told you to wait at the safehouse, I imagine. Promised he’d come back for you." 

Julian’s breath hitched. 

"Tell me where the ledger is, and I make sure Marcus never boards that flight. Stay silent, and you rot here while he spends your cut."

"The train station," Julian choked out. "Locker forty-two."

usuario: Write a conversation of up to 150 words between two people talking about something completely banal, while the reader understands perfectly that they are deciding the end of their relationship.
respuesta:
"Look at the ficus," she said, setting her mug on the counter. "The leaves are turning brown again."

He didn’t look up from his newspaper. "It never liked this corner. Not enough light."

"I've tried watering it more. I bought that expensive fertilizer you suggested. I even misted it." 

He sighed, folding the paper slowly. "Sometimes it doesn’t matter what you do, Sarah. Once the roots are bound, it just suffocates in the pot."

"We could repot it. Move it to the bedroom."

"We tried that in the spring, remember? It dropped half its leaves in a week. It’s just exhausting, sweeping them up every morning, pretending it’s going to bounce back."

She traced the rim of her cup, her voice dropping to a whisper. "So, what? We just throw it out?"

He finally met her eyes, his expression gentle, yet final. "You can take it, if you think it'll do better at a new place. Otherwise, yes. I think we just let it go."

usuario: Write a story of exactly 50 words that ends with the word "still".
respuesta: The ferocious storm battered the fragile wooden cabin. Outside, ancient pine trees snapped like brittle twigs under the howling gale. Inside, Sarah huddled closely beside the dying embers, clutching her shivering dog. She closed her eyes, praying for morning. Suddenly, the deafening wind vanished, leaving the snowy forest completely still.

usuario: Describe a protagonist in 100 to 150 words without mentioning any detail of their physical appearance (no clothes, height, eye or hair color): only through what they do and what they decide.
respuesta: Every morning, Julian arrives at the archives thirty minutes before the shift begins, choosing to spend the quiet hour memorizing the files slated for incineration. When a superior offers a lucrative promotion in exchange for overlooking a discrepancy in the city’s water ration logs, Julian declines without hesitation and secretly copies the fraudulent data onto an encrypted drive. At noon, rather than dining in the warm commissary, Julian walks three blocks to feed a stray dog waiting by the perimeter fence, dividing a meager lunch in half. Later, when trapped in the records room during a midnight security sweep, Julian decides against forcing the emergency exit. Instead, Julian remotely triggers a fire alarm on the opposite floor to draw the guards away, waiting patiently in the dark before delivering the stolen truth to the underground press.

usuario: Choose an everyday, insignificant object and write a lyric poem of up to twelve lines that treats it as if it were an archaeological treasure or a historic monument.
respuesta:
**The Pull-Tab**

Unearthed from dusty strata by the broom,
This twin-eyed amulet of silver gleams;
No marble vault or gilded pharaoh’s tomb
Could hoard a purer relic of our dreams.

Behold the sacred loop, the tiny pry
That once unsealed an effervescent sea!
What thirsty giant bent it with a sigh
To loose the hissed libation’s mystery?

Now severed from its vessel’s frigid crest,
This monument of alloy still remains:
An artifact of some forgotten quest,
The crown of carbonated, lost domains.

usuario: Choose a complex feeling and define it in up to 120 words using only visual metaphors and textures, without ever using the word that names it. At the end, in square brackets, say which feeling it is.
respuesta:
It is the frayed edge of a sun-bleached velvet quilt, plush yet thinning to bare, fragile threads. It is a room bathed in amber evening light, viewed through a thick pane of frosted, wavy glass—visibly glowing, yet cold and slick to the touch. It carries the rough grain of a creased sepia photograph and the weightless drift of golden dust motes suspended in a sunbeam, scattering at the slightest breeze. It is a handful of smooth, sun-warmed sea glass that slowly hardens into jagged, brittle ice against the palm. A vibrant path of crisp autumn leaves that instantly crumbles into fine, gray ash beneath the weight of a single footstep. 

[Nostalgia]

usuario: Write a micro-story of 40 to 80 words in which every word begins with the same letter.
respuesta:
Seven seasoned sailors sailed southward, seeking secret, shimmering seas. Suddenly, sinister storms struck. Savage swells smashed sturdy starboard sides; splintered spars scattered. Scared seamen scrambled, shouting senselessly. Six shipmates sank swiftly. 

Sole survivor Samuel swam stubbornly. Shivering, sore, Samuel sighted silver sands. Struggling shoreward, Samuel slumped, sighing softly. Soon, summer sunbeams shone, scattering shadows. Samuel stood, smiling, savoring sweet, surprising salvation.

usuario: Write a tense scene of up to 150 words between two characters in which one interrogates the other without using a single question mark: they must get the information using only statements or psychological manipulation.
respuesta:
Marcus set the heavy pliers on the table. Sweat beaded on Leo’s forehead.

"The syndicate thinks I took the ledger, Leo. They are five minutes away. When they arrive, I will hand them a thief."

Leo strained against the zip-ties. "I didn't touch it."

"Your fingernails are clean," Marcus noted softly, pacing the cramped room. "No mud from the yard. That means you never left this apartment. Yet your knuckles are scraped. Drywall dust clings to your cuffs."

Leo’s eyes darted involuntarily toward the hallway.

"A man only hides something in the walls if he plans to come back for it," Marcus whispered, picking up the pliers. "The syndicate won't search the drywall. They will just peel the answer off your fingers."

Leo broke, trembling violently. "Behind the fuse box. Wrapped in plastic. Just untie me."

usuario: Write a conversation of up to 150 words between two people talking about something completely banal, while the reader understands perfectly that they are deciding the end of their relationship.
respuesta:
“It’s making that choking sound again.”

“I know. I changed the filter, but it still comes out bitter.”

“We’ve had it six years, Mark. That’s a long run for a little machine.”

“Should I try to fix it? I still have the manual somewhere.”

“Honestly, we’d just be wasting our Sunday. The heating element is gone. It’s been coming out lukewarm for months.”

“I suppose so. We barely use it in the mornings anymore anyway. I usually just get mine on the way to work now.”

“Me too. It’s just taking up space in the kitchen. Making us feel guilty every time we look at it.”

“So, we just unplug it?”

“Yeah. Before the glass cracks and makes a mess neither of us wants to clean up.”

“Alright. You pull the plug. I’ll go get a box from the garage.”

usuario: Write a story of exactly 50 words that ends with the word "still".
respuesta: Heavy footsteps echoed down the dark hallway, getting closer to the closet. Sarah covered her mouth, praying the monster would not hear her pounding heart. Light seeped beneath the door as the shadow paused outside. A long claw scraped the wood. To survive the night, she had to remain still.
